'''David Erie Nadler''' (born 1973){{r|viaf}} is an American [[mathematician]] who specializes in geometric [[representation theory]] and [[symplectic geometry]].  He is currently a professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].{{r|berkeley}}{{r|cv}}

==Education and career==
Nadler graduated from [[Brown University]] with a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in mathematics in 1996.{{r|cv}}  He completed his doctoral studies at [[Princeton University]] under the supervision of [[Robert MacPherson (mathematician)|Robert MacPherson]], earning a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in mathematics in 2001.{{r|cv}}{{r|mathgen}}  He worked as an instructor at the [[University of Chicago]] for several years before taking a tenure track position at [[Northwestern University]] in 2005, where he became a Full Professor in 2011.{{r|cv}}{{r|nw}}  He moved to his current position at the University of California at Berkeley in 2012.{{r|berkeley}}

==Recognition==

In 2007 Nadler was selected as a [[Sloan Research Fellow]],{{r|sloan}} and in 2013 he became a member of the inaugural class of [[American Mathematical Society#Fellows|Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]].{{r|ams}}

Nadler delivered the [[Arf Lecture]] in 2012.{{r|arf}}
